profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a publicly traded semiconductor and computing company, founded in 1993 and headquartered in Santa Clara, CA. It trades on the exchange under the ticker NVDA and reported revenue of $215,938,000,000 for the fiscal year ending January 25, 2026, according to its most recent 10-K filing. The company operates across hardware, software, and AI platforms, with a significant focus on GPU-accelerated computing.

On the AI software side, NVIDIA offers the Nemotron family of multimodal foundation models, which the company describes as designed for long-running, self-evolving agents capable of reasoning, vision, speech, and retrieval-augmented generation tasks. The site highlights Nemotron 3.5 Lightning as a variant aimed at faster task completion, and NeMo Switchyard as a routing tool for directing workloads to appropriate models. NVIDIA publishes model weights, training datasets, and training techniques under the NVIDIA Open Model License, which permits use, modification, distribution, and commercial deployment without attribution. Nemotron models are available both as open-source downloads and as NVIDIA NIM microservices, the latter requiring an NVIDIA AI Enterprise license for secure, scalable deployment. Bryan Catanzaro, identified on the site as VP of applied deep learning research at NVIDIA, is noted as a voice behind the Nemotron vision.

The held facts confirm NVIDIA maintains two tracked AI products, Nemotron and NIM, and has a verified presence in the site's registry. No litigation or MCP server entries are recorded in the held data.
